# The D24 audio patch plan

55 patches, 63 measurements, 3 lead changes.

## This is a SHORT list

It is generated from the same source as the full one, with sockets left out on purpose. Nothing here was edited by hand.

* left out: MIC 1, MIC 13, MIC 14, MIC 15, MIC 16, MIC 2, MIC 3, MIC 4, every path that needs the XLR-F to 3.5 mm TRS
* patches the exclusions removed: 8
* AUX 2 now reads on MIC 11 (its own input is excluded)
* AUX 3 now reads on MIC 12 (its own input is excluded)
* AUX 4 now reads on MIC 17 (its own input is excluded)
* the TRS outputs now reads on MIC 5 (MIC 1 is excluded)

An output whose only test used a socket that was left out is MOVED onto an input that was carrying nothing but the parked output, so leaving an input out never quietly stops proving an output.

## The kit

| lead | what it is | how it is wired | patches |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | XLR-F to XLR-M | straight balanced: pin 1-1, 2-2, 3-3 | 17 |
| K5 | 150 ohm XLR-M terminator | 150 ohm across pins 2-3, pin 1 to the shell | 16 |
| K4 | XLR-F to 6.35 mm TRS | pin 2 -> tip, pin 3 -> ring, pin 1 -> sleeve | 16 |
| K2 | 6.35 mm TRS to XLR-M | tip -> pin 2, ring -> pin 3, sleeve -> pin 1 | 6 |

One of each. The order above is the order the station walks, so the operator changes lead type 3 times in a whole pass and never goes back to a lead already put down.

## The blocks

| # | lead | block | patches | measurements | the end that stays put |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | K1 | the microphone inputs | 17 | 17 | the input end walks all 17; the output end moves once per output for the first 10 and then stays on AUX 1 for the remaining 7 |
| 2 | K5 | the input noise rows | 16 | 16 | nothing: the terminator moves on its own |
| 3 | K4 | the line inputs | 16 | 16 | the output end, on AUX 1 |
| 4 | K2 | the TRS outputs | 6 | 14 | the input end, in MIC 5 |
